args.fidelityNote: Full fidelity is affordable: the repository's own Table-2 configs (PPI: 1000 epochs, dim 512, 1-0-1-0; Flickr: 15/30 epochs, dim 256, 1-1-0) run unmodified on one cheap GPU. Measured on a T4 with the verified launch recipe: PPI-Node 389 s wall (test F1-micro 0.9660 vs paper 0.960), PPI-RW 500 s (0.9815 vs 0.981), Flickr-RW 17 s (0.5098 vs 0.511), Flickr-Node 18 s (0.5010 vs 0.507). So all 8 claims (4 samplers x 2 datasets) are produced by single end-to-end training runs, one per config, no data/epoch reduction, and even the worst case (sum of timeouts = 9600 s) costs only ~$1.57 of the $4.98 budget. Two environment specifics are unavoidable and are baked into every stage command: (1) the Cython extension modules (cython_sampler / cython_utils / norm_aggr) cannot be built at run time because the image has no C/C++ compiler and package mirrors are blocked for network stages, so the engineer's prebuilt cpython-311 .so objects in /cache/gs_build are copied into graphsaint/ (checked: /cache/gs_build has 3 files); (2) graphsaint/utils.py loads './{prefix}/adj_full.npz', so data must be reachable at a repo-relative path - the fetched /cache/gdata/<dataset> dirs are symlinked to data/<dataset>. Datasets are fetched from the paper's Google Drive folder as direct per-file downloads (verified to return raw bytes, incl. the 357 MB flickr/feats.npy); they were also pre-populated now so the fetch step is idempotent. Each run is a fresh container, no checkpoints/resume needed since every stage is independent, and results are read from the final "Full test stats: F1_Micro" line (last match in the log). Note the repo has no seeding code, so each claim is a single stochastic run of the documented protocol; paper std is 0.001-0.007.

args.fidelityNote: Full fidelity fits the budget: the repo's own Table-2 configs run unmodified (PPI: 1000 epochs, dim 512, arch 1-0-1-0, 3000 roots / 4000 edges / 8000-node subgraphs; Flickr: 15-30 epochs, dim 256, arch 1-1-0). Measured end-to-end on a T4 with exactly the stage command: PPI-RW 500 s wall -> test F1-micro 0.9815 (paper 0.981±0.004); PPI-Node 389 s -> 0.9660 (0.960±0.001); Flickr-RW 17 s -> 0.5098/0.5072 (0.511±0.001); Flickr-Node 18 s -> 0.5010 (0.507±0.001). Sum of timeouts (worst case) = 4x1800 s + 4x600 s = 9600 s = $1.57 at T4 $0.59/h, i.e. well inside $4.98, so no epochs/data/model are reduced and absolute F1 values are the target. Each of the 8 claims is one independent end-to-end run of one documented sampler/dataset config (the repo has no seeding code, so a run is stochastic; paper std is 0.001-0.007), and the value is the last "Full test stats: F1_Micro" line. No stage depends on another: every stage is `python -m graphsaint.pytorch_version.train ...` (a repo module, no inline program) run fresh. Two environment facts (from the engineer's report, re-verified here) make a tiny idempotent glue necessary, supplied by PYTHONPATH=/cache/data/gs_setup whose sitecustomize.py runs at interpreter start: (1) graphsaint.cython_sampler / cython_utils / norm_aggr are imported unconditionally but cannot be built at run time (image has no C/C++ compiler, no make, package mirrors blocked), so the engineer's prebuilt cpython-311 .so objects kept in /cache/data/gs_build are copied into the graphsaint package (with a meta-path finder fallback that loads them straight from /cache/data/gs_build if the repo tree is read-only); (2) graphsaint/utils.py loads './{prefix}/adj_full.npz', so the fetched data is addressed as --data_prefix ../cache/data/<dataset> (verified: loads PPI/Flickr from /cache/data with cwd=/work) and the glue also links data/<dataset> for the README layout. Datasets come from the paper's Google Drive folder as direct per-file downloads (drive.usercontent.google.com returns raw bytes for all 10 files, including the 357 MB flickr/feats.npy); they are pre-populated so the fetch step is idempotent. Checks verify 5 files per dataset plus the 3 prebuilt extensions.
